title: The Two Watches
synopsis: Kim Gu and a young man named Yun Bong-gil ate breakfast together.
Then they swapped their watches. Which watch is which?
goal: Find out which watch Kim Gu holds, and what that morning meant.

options.label: Mr. Kim sits alone with a watch

notes: Haesu's note, read out of order with first, after, before that and at the end. Buying the watch is a decoy her note rules out (not this morning).
Breakfast, then the swap, is history (h2); Haesu, her note and the room are made up.

clueInputs.note: Kim Gu's case note: he trusts Haesu.

learning.objective: first, after breakfast, before that, at the end를 읽고 그날 아침의 네 장면을 순서대로 놓는다.
expressions: After breakfast, they swapped their watches.

play.title: Breakfast for Two
story: At the door, a young man in a grey suit passes you.
Inside, two rice bowls are empty on the table.
Under one bowl is a note with a small water drop.
play.letter:
At the end, Mr. Kim sat alone at the table, holding a watch.
Before that, Mr. Yun said goodbye.
They ate breakfast first, quietly.
After breakfast, they swapped their watches.
Mr. Yun's watch was new. He did not buy it this morning.
— a small water drop
play.question: Put the morning in order, from first to last.
hints: One line says what they did first.
At the end means the last step. Before that means just before it.
play.successMessage: You put the morning in order!
transition: Breakfast, the swap, goodbye, and Mr. Kim alone.
Haesu comes in from the kitchen with tea.
"Mr. Kim is still holding the watch. He has not said a word."
play.orderFeedback: Those are the right steps. Read first, after, before that and at the end again.

play.title: Which Watch?
story: Mr. Kim lays the watch in his hand on the table.
Haesu lays two more next to it: his old case and her own watch.
"Which one is his now?" she whispers.
play.letter:
Mr. Kim's old watch has a worn case with many small scratches.
Mr. Yun's watch is new. Its case is smooth, with no scratches.
My own watch is small, on a leather strap.
They swapped. Each man took the other's watch.

She brings out the old wooden box from Aunae.
It has a new lock with four letter tiles.

In Shanghai, I put a letter lock on our box.
Its word is our mark.
Every note in this box has the same small mark:
a small water drop. The lock wants the last word.

play.title: After That Day
story: Some weeks later, Haesu reads you a new page in her note.
Mr. Kim still keeps the new watch in his pocket.
"Everything changed after that morning," she says.
play.letter:
Our government began in Shanghai in nineteen nineteen.
On the twenty-ninth of April, nineteen thirty-two, Mr. Yun went to Hongkou Park.
He attacked a Japanese army ceremony there. He was arrested at once.
After that day, many Chinese people saw our fight in a new way.
Chinese leaders began to help our government strongly.

objectives: Find the watch Mr. Kim holds.
intro: Spring, 1932. You are a guest of Kim Gu in Shanghai again.
Haesu, the young clerk, now works close to him.
Early on 29 April, he asks you to come to a small house.
"A young man named Yun Bong-gil eats breakfast with me," he says.
play.caseSummary: On the morning of 29 April 1932, Yun Bong-gil and Kim Gu ate breakfast, then swapped watches. Yun left his new watch with Kim Gu and took the old one. Haesu kept the story in the keepers' box. That day Yun acted at Hongkou Park and was arrested. After it, Chinese leaders helped the Provisional Government strongly.

notes: PART 10 Case 10: set on the morning of 29 April 1932, around Yun Bong-gil's act, never in it. Haesu is the same keeper as Case 09 (one portrait, reused); Kim Gu's portrait is Case 09's.

Yun Bong-gil and Kim Gu are real; their words are made up (dossier fiction). Haesu, her notes, the strap watch and the box's lock are made up. The case ends on history: Chinese support for the Provisional Government after 29 April 1932 (h4); Yun's arrest and death are told once in the reveal.
